(Note) Al-Bayhaqi narrated from the hadith of Musa ibn Ubayda al-Rabadhi, from Sadaqa ibn Yasar, from Ibn Umar, who said: This surah, "When the help of Allah and the victory come" [al-Nasr 110:1], was revealed to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ in the middle of the days of tashriq, and it was recognized that it was the farewell. So he ordered his she-camel al-Qaswa to be saddled, and the people gathered, and he said: "O people," and then he mentioned the hadith in his sermon.

(Section) Umar ibn al-Khattab said to the Companions: "What do you say about the surah, 'When the help of Allah and the victory come'?"

They said: "Allah commanded His Prophet, when victory was granted to him, to seek His forgiveness." Then he said to Ibn Abbas: "What do you say?" He said: "It is the term (ajal) of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ; Allah informed him of it." Umar said: "I know nothing of it except what you know." This is one of the most subtle and refined understandings, which not everyone attains. For He, glorified be He, did not attach the seeking of forgiveness to his own deed, but attached it to the blessing He Himself produced: the granting of victory to His Messenger and the entry of people into His religion. This is not a cause for seeking forgiveness, so it is known that the cause of seeking forgiveness is something else, namely the approach of the term, which is part of the completion of Allah's blessing upon His servant: that He grants him success in sincere repentance and seeking forgiveness before Him, so that he meets his Lord pure and purified from every sin, and comes before Him joyful, content, and pleasing to Him.

This is also indicated by His saying: "So glorify with the praise of your Lord and seek His forgiveness" [al-Nasr 110:3], and he ﷺ always used to glorify Allah with His praise.

So it is known that what was commanded in that is glorification after the victory and the entry of people into this religion, a matter greater than that which preceded it, and that this is a preface before his transition to the Highest Companion (al-Rafiq al-A'la). There remained for him a portion of the servitude of glorification and seeking forgiveness, which elevates him to that station, so He commanded him to fulfil it. This is also indicated by the fact that He, glorified be He, prescribed repentance and seeking forgiveness at the ends of acts of worship: so He prescribed it at the conclusion of Hajj and of the night prayer.

"The Prophet ﷺ, when he finished the prayer, would seek forgiveness three times."

And it is prescribed for one who performs ablution, after completing his wudu, to say: "O Allah, make me of those who repent and make me of those who purify themselves."

So it is known that repentance is prescribed after righteous deeds. Thus He commanded His Messenger to seek forgiveness after he had fulfilled what was upon him of conveying the message and striving in His way, when people had entered His religion in multitudes. It is as if conveying was an act of worship which he had completed and performed, so seeking forgiveness was prescribed for him after it.

The purpose is that people differ in levels of understanding of the texts: among them is one who derives from the verse one or two rulings, and among them is one who derives from it ten rulings or more, and among them is one who restricts his understanding to the mere wording without its context, without its allusion, indication, admonition, and consideration. More specific than this and more subtle is joining it to another text related to it, so that from their conjunction one understands a measure beyond that wording taken alone. This is a wondrous door of understanding the Qur'an, which only the rare scholars notice, for the mind may not perceive the connection of this with that and its relation to it.

This is like what Ibn Abbas understood from His saying: "And his bearing and weaning are thirty months" [al-Ahqaf 46:15] together with His saying: "And mothers suckle their children for two complete years" [al-Baqarah 2:233]: that a woman may give birth after six months.

And like what al-Siddiq understood from the verses of inheritance at the beginning and end of the surah, that the kalalah is one who has neither child nor parent, and he excluded the brothers by the grandfather. The Prophet ﷺ had guided Umar to this understanding when he asked him about the kalalah and repeatedly returned to the question concerning it, and he said: "The verse of summer suffices you."

What was unclear to Umar was His saying: "Say: Allah gives you a ruling concerning the kalalah: if a man dies leaving no child" [al-Nisa 4:176].

The Prophet ﷺ then directed him to what clarifies its meaning for him, namely the first verse which was revealed in summer, for in it he assigned to the uterine sibling in the kalalah a sixth; and there is no doubt that the kalalah in it is one who has neither child nor parent, even if the ascendants go up.

And he said in (al-Madarij):

Understanding is a blessing from Allah upon His servant, and a light that Allah casts into his heart, by which he knows and perceives what others do not perceive or know, so he understands from the text what others do not understand, although both are equal in memorizing it and in understanding its basic meaning.

Understanding from Allah and His Messenger is the sign of sincerity (al-siddiqiyya) and the banner of prophetic guardianship (al-wilaya al-nabawiyya). In it the ranks of scholars differ, to the point that one is counted as a thousand. What Ibn Abbas was singled out for in understanding from it is that it was Allah's announcement to His Prophet of his death and His informing him of the approach of his term, and Umar's agreement with him on that, while it remained hidden from the other Companions, though Ibn Abbas at that time was the youngest of them in age. And where would you find in this surah the announcement of his term, were it not for the special understanding? This subtlety reaches levels which the understandings of most people fall short of, so that one needs something besides the text; and for him there is no reliance on texts alone, whereas for the one possessing understanding, he does not need anything beyond the texts alongside them.

(Note) He said regarding the surah of the term of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, which is the last surah revealed: "When the help of Allah and the victory come, and you see people entering the religion of Allah in multitudes, then glorify with the praise of your Lord and seek His forgiveness; indeed He is ever Accepting of repentance" [al-Nasr 110:1–3].

In the two Sahihs, from Aisha, may Allah be pleased with her, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ did not pray any prayer after this surah was revealed to him without saying in his bowing and prostration: "Glory be to You, O Allah, our Lord, and with Your praise. O Allah, forgive me," interpreting the Qur'an.

Repentance is thus the ultimate end of every wayfarer and every friend of Allah, and it is the goal toward which those who know Allah and His servitude proceed, and what befits Him. Allah, the Exalted, said: "Indeed, We offered the trust to the heavens and the earth and the mountains, but they refused to bear it and feared it, and man bore it; indeed he was unjust and ignorant" — "so that Allah may punish the hypocrite men and hypocrite women and the polytheist men and polytheist women, and Allah may accept the repentance of the believing men and believing women; and Allah is ever Forgiving and Merciful" [al-Ahzab 33:72–73].

So He, glorified be He, made repentance the goal of every believing man and believing woman.

(Section) In the Sahih, from him ﷺ, that he said: "O people, repent to Allah, for by Allah I repent to Him more than seventy times a day." And his Companions would count for him in a single sitting, before he rose, "My Lord, forgive me and accept my repentance, indeed You are the Accepting, the Forgiving" one hundred times. And he never prayed a prayer after "When the help of Allah and the victory come" was revealed to him, to its end, without saying in it: "Glory be to You, O Allah, our Lord, and with Your praise. O Allah, forgive me."

It is authentically related from him ﷺ that he said: "No one among you will be saved by his deeds." They said: "Not even you, O Messenger of Allah?" He said: "Not even I, unless Allah covers me with His mercy and grace."

So may the blessings and peace of Allah be upon the one most knowledgeable of creation about Allah, His rights, His greatness, what His majesty deserves of servitude, and the most knowing of them of servitude and its rights, and the most steadfast of them in it.

(Section) When the Messenger of Allah came out from the siege of the enemy, he entered the siege of victory. The hands of his expeditions wrought victory in the outlying regions, and his mention flew across the horizons, so creation with him became three categories: a believer in him, one at peace with him, and one fearful of him. He cast the seed of patience into a field: "So be patient as the steadfast of the messengers were patient" [al-Ahqaf 46:35]. Then behold, the shoots of plants swayed with fragrant blossoms, and the sacred prohibitions became retaliation. So he entered Mecca with an entry no one entered before him or after him: the emigrants and the helpers surrounded him, of whom only the pupils of the eyes could be seen; the Companions were in their ranks, the angels above their heads, and Gabriel moved between him and his Lord. And He had made lawful for him His sanctuary which He had not made lawful for anyone besides him. When he compared this day with the day of "And when those who disbelieved schemed to confine you, or kill you, or expel you" so that they expelled him, "the second of two" [al-Anfal 8:30; al-Tawba 9:40].

He entered with his chin nearly touching the saddle's pommel, in humility and submission to Him who clothed him in this garment of honor, toward which creation raised its heads and kings stretched their necks. So he entered Mecca as a possessor, aided and victorious.

Bilal ascended above the Ka'ba after he had been dragged on the scorching sand over the embers of trial. He spread out a fine cloth that had been folded from the people since the day of his saying "One, One."

He raised his voice with the adhan, and the tribes answered from every direction, coming toward the sound, and they entered the religion of Allah in multitudes, whereas before that they had come individually. When the Messenger sat on the pulpit of honor, he never descended from it.

Kings stretched their necks in submission to him: some handed him the keys of their lands, some asked him for truce and reconciliation, some acknowledged the jizya and humiliation, and some began gathering and preparing for war, not realizing that he had only been gathering spoils and driving captives to him.

When his victory was complete, he had conveyed the message and fulfilled the trust, and there came to him the decree: "Indeed We have granted you a manifest victory, that Allah may forgive you what preceded of your sin and what follows, complete His favor upon you, guide you to a straight path, and help you with a mighty help" [al-Fath 48:1–3].

After it came the signature: "When the help of Allah and the victory come, and you see people entering the religion of Allah in multitudes."

His Lord's messenger came to him informing him of the choice between remaining in this world and meeting Him; so he chose the meeting with his Lord, out of longing for Him. The gardens were adorned for the day of the arrival of his noble soul, not like the adornment of Medina on the day a king arrives.

If the Throne of the Merciful trembled with joy and gladness at the death of some of His followers, welcoming their souls, then how about the soul of the master of creation?!

O you who claim affiliation to other than this threshold, and you who stand at other than this door, you will know on the Day of Gathering what secret you will have: "The day when secrets are tested" [al-Tariq 86:9].

(Section: on the explanation that Mecca was conquered by force)

(Section)
In it is clear evidence that Mecca was conquered by force (ʿanwatan), as the majority of scholars held. No dissent is known on this except from al-Shafi'i and, in one of his two opinions, Ahmad. The context of the story is the clearest proof for one who reflects on it for the majority's view. When Abu Hamid al-Ghazali found fault with the claim that it was conquered by treaty (sulh), he related al-Shafi'i's view that it was conquered by force in his "Wasit," and said: "This is his school."

The proponents of treaty said: "Had it been conquered by force, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ would have divided it among the fighters, as he divided Khaybar, and as he divided the rest of the movable spoils. He would have fifth-ed and distributed them." They said: "When Abu Sufyan sought safe-conduct for the people of Mecca when he embraced Islam, and he granted it to them, this was a treaty agreement with them." They said: "Had it been conquered by force, the victors would have owned its homes and houses, and they would have had more right to them than their owners, and it would have been permissible to expel them from it. Since the Messenger of Allah ﷺ did not rule regarding it by this ruling, but did not even return to the emigrants their houses from which they had been expelled, which were in the hands of those who had expelled them, and he permitted them to sell, buy, rent, live in, and benefit from the houses, this contradicts the rulings of conquest by force. He explicitly attributed the houses to their owners, saying: 'Whoever enters the house of Abu Sufyan is safe, and whoever enters his own house is safe.'"

The proponents of force said: "Had he made a treaty with them, his safe-conduct, restricted to each person entering his house, closing his door, and laying down his weapon, would have had no purpose. Khalid ibn al-Walid would not have fought them until he killed a group of them, and he would not have been rebuked for it. When Muqays ibn Subaba and Abdullah ibn Khatal and those mentioned with them were killed, had a treaty contract been concluded, these would certainly have been excepted in it, and this and that would have been transmitted. Had it been conquered by treaty, he would not have fought them, and he had said: 'If anyone takes license to fight the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, say: Indeed Allah permitted His Messenger, and did not permit you.' It is well known that this permission specific to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ is permission to fight, not to make peace, for permission to make peace is general."

Also: had its conquest been by treaty, he would not have said that Allah had made it lawful for him for an hour of the day. For if it had been conquered by treaty, it would have remained in its sanctity and would not have left its sanctity by treaty. He informed that in that hour it was not forbidden, and that after the hour of battle ended it returned to its original sanctity.

Also, if it had been conquered by treaty, he would not have arrayed his army, cavalry and infantry, on the right and left flanks, with weapons in their hands. He said to Abu Hurayrah: "Call the Ansar for me," so he called them and they came, and they surrounded the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. He said: "Do you see the rabble of Quraysh and their followers?" Then he said, placing one hand upon the other: "Mow them down completely until you meet me at al-Safa." Until Abu Sufyan said: "O Messenger of Allah, the green of Quraysh has been made lawful (for slaughter); there is no Quraysh after today." The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Whoever closes his door is safe."

This cannot be the case with a treaty. If a treaty had preceded it, and no (it did not), it would have been annulled by this (anyway).

Also, how could it be a treaty when it was conquered only by the pressing of horses and riding beasts? Allah did not withhold the horses and riding beasts of His Messenger from it, as He withheld them on the day of the Treaty of al-Hudaybiyyah. For that day was truly a day of treaty. When al-Qaswa' knelt down with him, they said: "al-Qaswa' has balked." He said:
"She has not balked, and that is not her habit, but the One who withholds the elephant has withheld her."
Then he said: "By Allah, they will not ask me for any arrangement in which they honour one of the sacred things of Allah except that I will grant it to them."

Likewise, the treaty was concluded with a written document and witnesses, in the presence of an assembly of Muslims and polytheists, and the Muslims that day were one thousand four hundred. Yet such a treaty did not take place on the day of the Conquest; it was not written down, nor was witness borne to it, nor did anyone attend it, nor has its manner or its conditions been transmitted. This is a clearly impossible thing.

Consider his words: "Allah withheld the elephant from Mecca and gave power over it to His Messenger and the believers." How can it be understood from this that the subjugation of His Messenger and his conquering army over its people was greater than the subjugation of the elephant, which was going to enter it against them by force? So He withheld it from them, and gave His Messenger and the believers power over them, until they conquered it by force after subjugation and the authority of force, and the humbling of disbelief and its people. That was greater in worth, more momentous, more manifest as a sign, more complete in victory, and more exalted in word than to bring them under the bondage of a treaty, the dictates and conditions of the enemy, and to deprive them of the authority, might and triumph of force, in the greatest conquest that He granted to His Messenger, by which He honoured His religion and made it a sign to all the worlds.

They said: As for your statement that if it had been conquered by force it would have been divided among the victors, this is based on the premise that land is included among the spoils which Allah, glorified is He, ordered to be divided among the victors after a fifth is set aside. But the majority of the Companions and the imams after them held otherwise: that land is not included among the spoils that must be divided. This was the practice of the rightly-guided Caliphs. When Bilal and his companions asked Umar ibn al-Khattab, may Allah be pleased with him, to divide among them the land that had been conquered by force, namely the Levant and what surrounds it, and they said to him, "Take its fifth and divide it," Umar said: "This is other than wealth; rather, I will keep it as fay' that flows to you and to the Muslims." Bilal and his companions, may Allah be pleased with them, said: "Divide it among us." Umar said:
"O Allah, suffice me against Bilal and his kin." Not a year had passed before not one of them was left with an eye that blinked. Then all the rest of the Companions, may Allah be pleased with them, agreed with Umar, may Allah be pleased with him, on this. Likewise it was done in the conquests of Egypt, Iraq, the land of Persia, and all the other lands conquered by force: the rightly-guided Caliphs did not divide a single village from them.

It is not valid to say that he gained their consent and made it a waqf with their agreement, for they disputed with him over this, and he refused them, and he prayed against Bilal and his companions, may Allah be pleased with them. What he saw and did was the very right course and pure success, for had it been divided, its heirs and their relatives would have inherited it, and the village and the land would have passed to a single woman or a small child, while the fighting men would have had nothing in their hands. In that would have been the greatest and gravest corruption, and this is what Umar, may Allah be pleased with him, feared. So Allah, glorified is He, granted him success in leaving the land undivided and making it a waqf for the fighting men, flowing to them as fay' until the last of the Muslims should raid from it. The blessing of his opinion and its good fortune for Islam and its people became manifest, and the majority of the imams agreed with him. They differed over how it should be kept undivided. The apparent position of Imam Ahmad and most of his texts is that the imam has discretion over it, a discretion of public interest, not of desire: if dividing it is best for the Muslims, he divides it; if making it a waqf for their community is best, he makes it a waqf; if dividing part and making part waqf is best, he does so. For the Messenger of Allah ﷺ did all three: he divided the land of Qurayzah and al-Nadir, left Mecca undivided, divided part of Khaybar and left part of it for what fell to him of the public interests of the Muslims.

There is a second narration from Ahmad, that it becomes waqf by the very fact of its being taken and seized, without the imam establishing it as waqf; this is the position of Malik.

And there is a third narration from him: that he divides it among the victors as he divides the movable property among them, unless they relinquish their rights in it; this is the position of al-Shafi'i.

Abu Hanifah said: The imam has discretion between dividing it, or leaving its owners in possession of it under kharaj, or expelling them from it and sending other people to it, upon whom he imposes kharaj.

What Umar did, may Allah be pleased with him, is not contrary to the Qur'an, for land is not included among the spoils which Allah commanded to be fifth-divided and divided. For this reason Umar said: "It is other than wealth." This is shown by the fact that the permission of spoils was not granted to any nation other than this Ummah; rather, it is among its distinguishing features, as he ﷺ said in the hadith agreed upon as authentic: "Spoils have been made lawful for me, and they were not lawful for anyone before me."

Allah, glorified is He, had made lawful the land that was in the hands of the disbelievers for those before us, the followers of the messengers, when they seized it by force, as He made it lawful for the people of Moses. Hence Moses said to his people: ﴿O my people, enter the holy land which Allah has prescribed for you, and do not turn back on your heels, lest you turn about as losers﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 21].

Moses and his people fought the disbelievers, seized their lands and wealth, and gathered the spoils; then fire came down from heaven and consumed them, and they dwelt in the land and the homes, and these were not forbidden to them. It is thus known that land is not among the spoils, and that it belongs to Allah, Who bequeaths it to whom He wills.

(Note) Al-Bayhaqi narrated from the hadith of Musa ibn Ubayda al-Rabadhi, from Sadaqa ibn Yasar, from Ibn Umar, who said: This surah, "When the help of Allah and the victory come" [al-Nasr 110:1], was revealed to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ in the middle of the days of tashriq, and it was recognized that it was the farewell. Bilal ascended above the Ka'ba after he had been dragged on the scorching sand over the embers of trial. He spread out a fine cloth that had been folded from the people since the day of his saying "One, One."

He raised his voice with the adhan, and the tribes answered from every direction, coming toward the sound, and they entered the religion of Allah in multitudes, whereas before that they had come individually. When the Messenger sat on the pulpit of honor, he never descended from it.

Kings stretched their necks in submission to him: some handed him the keys of their lands, some asked him for truce and reconciliation, some acknowledged the jizya and humiliation, and some began gathering and preparing for war, not realizing that he had only been gathering spoils and driving captives to him.

When his victory was complete, he had conveyed the message and fulfilled the trust, and there came to him the decree: "Indeed We have granted you a manifest victory, that Allah may forgive you what preceded of your sin and what follows, complete His favor upon you, guide you to a straight path, and help you with a mighty help" [al-Fath 48:1–3].

After it came the signature: "When the help of Allah and the victory come, and you see people entering the religion of Allah in multitudes."

His Lord's messenger came to him informing him of the choice between remaining in this world and meeting Him; so he chose the meeting with his Lord, out of longing for Him. The gardens were adorned for the day of the arrival of his noble soul, not like the adornment of Medina on the day a king arrives.

If the Throne of the Merciful trembled with joy and gladness at the death of some of His followers, welcoming their souls, then how about the soul of the master of creation?!

O you who claim affiliation to other than this threshold, and you who stand at other than this door, you will know on the Day of Gathering what secret you will have: "The day when secrets are tested" [al-Tariq 86:9].

(Section: on the explanation that Mecca was conquered by force)

(Section)
In it is clear evidence that Mecca was conquered by force (ʿanwatan), as the majority of scholars held. No dissent is known on this except from al-Shafi'i and, in one of his two opinions, Ahmad. The context of the story is the clearest proof for one who reflects on it for the majority's view. When Abu Hamid al-Ghazali found fault with the claim that it was conquered by treaty (sulh), he related al-Shafi'i's view that it was conquered by force in his "Wasit," and said: "This is his school."

The proponents of treaty said: "Had it been conquered by force, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ would have divided it among the fighters, as he divided Khaybar, and as he divided the rest of the movable spoils. He would have fifth-ed and distributed them." They said: "When Abu Sufyan sought safe-conduct for the people of Mecca when he embraced Islam, and he granted it to them, this was a treaty agreement with them." They said: "Had it been conquered by force, the victors would have owned its homes and houses, and they would have had more right to them than their owners, and it would have been permissible to expel them from it. Since the Messenger of Allah ﷺ did not rule regarding it by this ruling, but did not even return to the emigrants their houses from which they had been expelled, which were in the hands of those who had expelled them, and he permitted them to sell, buy, rent, live in, and benefit from the houses, this contradicts the rulings of conquest by force. He explicitly attributed the houses to their owners, saying: 'Whoever enters the house of Abu Sufyan is safe, and whoever enters his own house is safe.'"

The proponents of force said: "Had he made a treaty with them, his safe-conduct, restricted to each person entering his house, closing his door, and laying down his weapon, would have had no purpose. Khalid ibn al-Walid would not have fought them until he killed a group of them, and he would not have been rebuked for it. When Muqays ibn Subaba and Abdullah ibn Khatal and those mentioned with them were killed, had a treaty contract been concluded, these would certainly have been excepted in it, and this and that would have been transmitted. Had it been conquered by treaty, he would not have fought them, and he had said: 'If anyone takes license to fight the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, say: Indeed Allah permitted His Messenger, and did not permit you.' It is well known that this permission specific to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ is permission to fight, not to make peace, for permission to make peace is general."

Also: had its conquest been by treaty, he would not have said that Allah had made it lawful for him for an hour of the day. For if it had been conquered by treaty, it would have remained in its sanctity and would not have left its sanctity by treaty. He informed that in that hour it was not forbidden, and that after the hour of battle ended it returned to its original sanctity.

Also, if it had been conquered by treaty, he would not have arrayed his army, cavalry and infantry, on the right and left flanks, with weapons in their hands. He said to Abu Hurayrah: "Call the Ansar for me," so he called them and they came, and they surrounded the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. He said: "Do you see the rabble of Quraysh and their followers?" Then he said, placing one hand upon the other: "Mow them down completely until you meet me at al-Safa." Until Abu Sufyan said: "O Messenger of Allah, the green of Quraysh has been made lawful (for slaughter); there is no Quraysh after today." The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Whoever closes his door is safe."

This cannot be the case with a treaty. If a treaty had preceded it, and no (it did not), it would have been annulled by this (anyway).

Also, how could it be a treaty when it was conquered only by the pressing of horses and riding beasts? Allah did not withhold the horses and riding beasts of His Messenger from it, as He withheld them on the day of the Treaty of al-Hudaybiyyah. For that day was truly a day of treaty. When al-Qaswa' knelt down with him, they said: "al-Qaswa' has balked." He said:
"She has not balked, and that is not her habit, but the One who withholds the elephant has withheld her."
Then he said: "By Allah, they will not ask me for any arrangement in which they honour one of the sacred things of Allah except that I will grant it to them."

Likewise, the treaty was concluded with a written document and witnesses, in the presence of an assembly of Muslims and polytheists, and the Muslims that day were one thousand four hundred. Yet such a treaty did not take place on the day of the Conquest; it was not written down, nor was witness borne to it, nor did anyone attend it, nor has its manner or its conditions been transmitted. This is a clearly impossible thing.

Consider his words: "Allah withheld the elephant from Mecca and gave power over it to His Messenger and the believers." How can it be understood from this that the subjugation of His Messenger and his conquering army over its people was greater than the subjugation of the elephant, which was going to enter it against them by force? So He withheld it from them, and gave His Messenger and the believers power over them, until they conquered it by force after subjugation and the authority of force, and the humbling of disbelief and its people. That was greater in worth, more momentous, more manifest as a sign, more complete in victory, and more exalted in word than to bring them under the bondage of a treaty, the dictates and conditions of the enemy, and to deprive them of the authority, might and triumph of force, in the greatest conquest that He granted to His Messenger, by which He honoured His religion and made it a sign to all the worlds.

They said: As for your statement that if it had been conquered by force it would have been divided among the victors, this is based on the premise that land is included among the spoils which Allah, glorified is He, ordered to be divided among the victors after a fifth is set aside. But the majority of the Companions and the imams after them held otherwise: that land is not included among the spoils that must be divided. This was the practice of the rightly-guided Caliphs. When Bilal and his companions asked Umar ibn al-Khattab, may Allah be pleased with him, to divide among them the land that had been conquered by force, namely the Levant and what surrounds it, and they said to him, "Take its fifth and divide it," Umar said: "This is other than wealth; rather, I will keep it as fay' that flows to you and to the Muslims." Bilal and his companions, may Allah be pleased with them, said: "Divide it among us." Umar said:
"O Allah, suffice me against Bilal and his kin." Not a year had passed before not one of them was left with an eye that blinked. Then all the rest of the Companions, may Allah be pleased with them, agreed with Umar, may Allah be pleased with him, on this. Likewise it was done in the conquests of Egypt, Iraq, the land of Persia, and all the other lands conquered by force: the rightly-guided Caliphs did not divide a single village from them.

It is not valid to say that he gained their consent and made it a waqf with their agreement, for they disputed with him over this, and he refused them, and he prayed against Bilal and his companions, may Allah be pleased with them. What he saw and did was the very right course and pure success, for had it been divided, its heirs and their relatives would have inherited it, and the village and the land would have passed to a single woman or a small child, while the fighting men would have had nothing in their hands. In that would have been the greatest and gravest corruption, and this is what Umar, may Allah be pleased with him, feared. So Allah, glorified is He, granted him success in leaving the land undivided and making it a waqf for the fighting men, flowing to them as fay' until the last of the Muslims should raid from it. The blessing of his opinion and its good fortune for Islam and its people became manifest, and the majority of the imams agreed with him. They differed over how it should be kept undivided. The apparent position of Imam Ahmad and most of his texts is that the imam has discretion over it, a discretion of public interest, not of desire: if dividing it is best for the Muslims, he divides it; if making it a waqf for their community is best, he makes it a waqf; if dividing part and making part waqf is best, he does so. For the Messenger of Allah ﷺ did all three: he divided the land of Qurayzah and al-Nadir, left Mecca undivided, divided part of Khaybar and left part of it for what fell to him of the public interests of the Muslims.

There is a second narration from Ahmad, that it becomes waqf by the very fact of its being taken and seized, without the imam establishing it as waqf; this is the position of Malik.

And there is a third narration from him: that he divides it among the victors as he divides the movable property among them, unless they relinquish their rights in it; this is the position of al-Shafi'i.

Abu Hanifah said: The imam has discretion between dividing it, or leaving its owners in possession of it under kharaj, or expelling them from it and sending other people to it, upon whom he imposes kharaj.

What Umar did, may Allah be pleased with him, is not contrary to the Qur'an, for land is not included among the spoils which Allah commanded to be fifth-divided and divided. For this reason Umar said: "It is other than wealth." This is shown by the fact that the permission of spoils was not granted to any nation other than this Ummah; rather, it is among its distinguishing features, as he ﷺ said in the hadith agreed upon as authentic: "Spoils have been made lawful for me, and they were not lawful for anyone before me."

Allah, glorified is He, had made lawful the land that was in the hands of the disbelievers for those before us, the followers of the messengers, when they seized it by force, as He made it lawful for the people of Moses. Hence Moses said to his people: ﴿O my people, enter the holy land which Allah has prescribed for you, and do not turn back on your heels, lest you turn about as losers﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 21].

Moses and his people fought the disbelievers, seized their lands and wealth, and gathered the spoils; then fire came down from heaven and consumed them, and they dwelt in the land and the homes, and these were not forbidden to them. It is thus known that land is not among the spoils, and that it belongs to Allah, Who bequeaths it to whom He wills.

(Note) Al-Bayhaqi narrated from the hadith of Musa ibn Ubayda al-Rabadhi, from Sadaqa ibn Yasar, from Ibn Umar, who said: This surah, "When the help of Allah and the victory come" [al-Nasr 110:1], was revealed to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ in the middle of the days of tashriq, and it was recognized that it was the farewell. So he ordered his she-camel al-Qaswa to be saddled, and the people gathered, and he said: "O people," and then he mentioned the hadith in his sermon.

(Section) Umar ibn al-Khattab said to the Companions: "What do you say about the surah, 'When the help of Allah and the victory come'?"

They said: "Allah commanded His Prophet, when victory was granted to him, to seek His forgiveness." Then he said to Ibn Abbas: "What do you say?" He said: "It is the term (ajal) of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ; Allah informed him of it." Umar said: "I know nothing of it except what you know." This is one of the most subtle and refined understandings, which not everyone attains. For He, glorified be He, did not attach the seeking of forgiveness to his own deed, but attached it to the blessing He Himself produced: the granting of victory to His Messenger and the entry of people into His religion. This is not a cause for seeking forgiveness, so it is known that the cause of seeking forgiveness is something else, namely the approach of the term, which is part of the completion of Allah's blessing upon His servant: that He grants him success in sincere repentance and seeking forgiveness before Him, so that he meets his Lord pure and purified from every sin, and comes before Him joyful, content, and pleasing to Him.

This is also indicated by His saying: "So glorify with the praise of your Lord and seek His forgiveness" [al-Nasr 110:3], and he ﷺ always used to glorify Allah with His praise.

So it is known that what was commanded in that is glorification after the victory and the entry of people into this religion, a matter greater than that which preceded it, and that this is a preface before his transition to the Highest Companion (al-Rafiq al-A'la). There remained for him a portion of the servitude of glorification and seeking forgiveness, which elevates him to that station, so He commanded him to fulfil it. This is also indicated by the fact that He, glorified be He, prescribed repentance and seeking forgiveness at the ends of acts of worship: so He prescribed it at the conclusion of Hajj and of the night prayer.

"The Prophet ﷺ, when he finished the prayer, would seek forgiveness three times."

And it is prescribed for one who performs ablution, after completing his wudu, to say: "O Allah, make me of those who repent and make me of those who purify themselves."

So it is known that repentance is prescribed after righteous deeds. Thus He commanded His Messenger to seek forgiveness after he had fulfilled what was upon him of conveying the message and striving in His way, when people had entered His religion in multitudes. It is as if conveying was an act of worship which he had completed and performed, so seeking forgiveness was prescribed for him after it.

The purpose is that people differ in levels of understanding of the texts: among them is one who derives from the verse one or two rulings, and among them is one who derives from it ten rulings or more, and among them is one who restricts his understanding to the mere wording without its context, without its allusion, indication, admonition, and consideration. More specific than this and more subtle is joining it to another text related to it, so that from their conjunction one understands a measure beyond that wording taken alone. This is a wondrous door of understanding the Qur'an, which only the rare scholars notice, for the mind may not perceive the connection of this with that and its relation to it.

This is like what Ibn Abbas understood from His saying: "And his bearing and weaning are thirty months" [al-Ahqaf 46:15] together with His saying: "And mothers suckle their children for two complete years" [al-Baqarah 2:233]: that a woman may give birth after six months.

And like what al-Siddiq understood from the verses of inheritance at the beginning and end of the surah, that the kalalah is one who has neither child nor parent, and he excluded the brothers by the grandfather. The Prophet ﷺ had guided Umar to this understanding when he asked him about the kalalah and repeatedly returned to the question concerning it, and he said: "The verse of summer suffices you."

What was unclear to Umar was His saying: "Say: Allah gives you a ruling concerning the kalalah: if a man dies leaving no child" [al-Nisa 4:176].

The Prophet ﷺ then directed him to what clarifies its meaning for him, namely the first verse which was revealed in summer, for in it he assigned to the uterine sibling in the kalalah a sixth; and there is no doubt that the kalalah in it is one who has neither child nor parent, even if the ascendants go up.

And he said in (al-Madarij):

Understanding is a blessing from Allah upon His servant, and a light that Allah casts into his heart, by which he knows and perceives what others do not perceive or know, so he understands from the text what others do not understand, although both are equal in memorizing it and in understanding its basic meaning.

Understanding from Allah and His Messenger is the sign of sincerity (al-siddiqiyya) and the banner of prophetic guardianship (al-wilaya al-nabawiyya). In it the ranks of scholars differ, to the point that one is counted as a thousand. Consider the understanding of Ibn Abbas when Umar asked him, and those present of the people of Badr and others, about the surah "When the help of Allah and the victory come."

What Ibn Abbas was singled out for in understanding from it is that it was Allah's announcement to His Prophet of his death and His informing him of the approach of his term, and Umar's agreement with him on that, while it remained hidden from the other Companions, though Ibn Abbas at that time was the youngest of them in age. And where would you find in this surah the announcement of his term, were it not for the special understanding? This subtlety reaches levels which the understandings of most people fall short of, so that one needs something besides the text; and for him there is no reliance on texts alone, whereas for the one possessing understanding, he does not need anything beyond the texts alongside them.

(Note) He said regarding the surah of the term of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, which is the last surah revealed: "When the help of Allah and the victory come, and you see people entering the religion of Allah in multitudes, then glorify with the praise of your Lord and seek His forgiveness; indeed He is ever Accepting of repentance" [al-Nasr 110:1–3].

In the two Sahihs, from Aisha, may Allah be pleased with her, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ did not pray any prayer after this surah was revealed to him without saying in his bowing and prostration: "Glory be to You, O Allah, our Lord, and with Your praise. O Allah, forgive me," interpreting the Qur'an.

Repentance is thus the ultimate end of every wayfarer and every friend of Allah, and it is the goal toward which those who know Allah and His servitude proceed, and what befits Him. Allah, the Exalted, said: "Indeed, We offered the trust to the heavens and the earth and the mountains, but they refused to bear it and feared it, and man bore it; indeed he was unjust and ignorant" — "so that Allah may punish the hypocrite men and hypocrite women and the polytheist men and polytheist women, and Allah may accept the repentance of the believing men and believing women; and Allah is ever Forgiving and Merciful" [al-Ahzab 33:72–73].

So He, glorified be He, made repentance the goal of every believing man and believing woman.

(Section) In the Sahih, from him ﷺ, that he said: "O people, repent to Allah, for by Allah I repent to Him more than seventy times a day." And his Companions would count for him in a single sitting, before he rose, "My Lord, forgive me and accept my repentance, indeed You are the Accepting, the Forgiving" one hundred times. And he never prayed a prayer after "When the help of Allah and the victory come" was revealed to him, to its end, without saying in it: "Glory be to You, O Allah, our Lord, and with Your praise. O Allah, forgive me."

It is authentically related from him ﷺ that he said: "No one among you will be saved by his deeds." They said: "Not even you, O Messenger of Allah?" He said: "Not even I, unless Allah covers me with His mercy and grace."

So may the blessings and peace of Allah be upon the one most knowledgeable of creation about Allah, His rights, His greatness, what His majesty deserves of servitude, and the most knowing of them of servitude and its rights, and the most steadfast of them in it.

(Section) When the Messenger of Allah came out from the siege of the enemy, he entered the siege of victory. The hands of his expeditions wrought victory in the outlying regions, and his mention flew across the horizons, so creation with him became three categories: a believer in him, one at peace with him, and one fearful of him. He cast the seed of patience into a field: "So be patient as the steadfast of the messengers were patient" [al-Ahqaf 46:35]. Then behold, the shoots of plants swayed with fragrant blossoms, and the sacred prohibitions became retaliation. So he entered Mecca with an entry no one entered before him or after him: the emigrants and the helpers surrounded him, of whom only the pupils of the eyes could be seen; the Companions were in their ranks, the angels above their heads, and Gabriel moved between him and his Lord. And He had made lawful for him His sanctuary which He had not made lawful for anyone besides him. When he compared this day with the day of "And when those who disbelieved schemed to confine you, or kill you, or expel you" so that they expelled him, "the second of two" [al-Anfal 8:30; al-Tawba 9:40].

He entered with his chin nearly touching the saddle's pommel, in humility and submission to Him who clothed him in this garment of honor, toward which creation raised its heads and kings stretched their necks. So he entered Mecca as a possessor, aided and victorious.

When his victory was complete, he had conveyed the message and fulfilled the trust, and there came to him the decree: "Indeed We have granted you a manifest victory, that Allah may forgive you what preceded of your sin and what follows, complete His favor upon you, guide you to a straight path, and help you with a mighty help" [al-Fath 48:1–3].

After it came the signature: "When the help of Allah and the victory come, and you see people entering the religion of Allah in multitudes."

His Lord's messenger came to him informing him of the choice between remaining in this world and meeting Him; so he chose the meeting with his Lord, out of longing for Him. The gardens were adorned for the day of the arrival of his noble soul, not like the adornment of Medina on the day a king arrives.

If the Throne of the Merciful trembled with joy and gladness at the death of some of His followers, welcoming their souls, then how about the soul of the master of creation?!

O you who claim affiliation to other than this threshold, and you who stand at other than this door, you will know on the Day of Gathering what secret you will have: "The day when secrets are tested" [al-Tariq 86:9].

In that would have been the greatest and gravest corruption, and this is what Umar, may Allah be pleased with him, feared. So Allah, glorified is He, granted him success in leaving the land undivided and making it a waqf for the fighting men, flowing to them as fay' until the last of the Muslims should raid from it. The blessing of his opinion and its good fortune for Islam and its people became manifest, and the majority of the imams agreed with him. They differed over how it should be kept undivided. The apparent position of Imam Ahmad and most of his texts is that the imam has discretion over it, a discretion of public interest, not of desire: if dividing it is best for the Muslims, he divides it; if making it a waqf for their community is best, he makes it a waqf; if dividing part and making part waqf is best, he does so. For the Messenger of Allah ﷺ did all three: he divided the land of Qurayzah and al-Nadir, left Mecca undivided, divided part of Khaybar and left part of it for what fell to him of the public interests of the Muslims.

There is a second narration from Ahmad, that it becomes waqf by the very fact of its being taken and seized, without the imam establishing it as waqf; this is the position of Malik.

And there is a third narration from him: that he divides it among the victors as he divides the movable property among them, unless they relinquish their rights in it; this is the position of al-Shafi'i.

Abu Hanifah said: The imam has discretion between dividing it, or leaving its owners in possession of it under kharaj, or expelling them from it and sending other people to it, upon whom he imposes kharaj.

What Umar did, may Allah be pleased with him, is not contrary to the Qur'an, for land is not included among the spoils which Allah commanded to be fifth-divided and divided. For this reason Umar said: "It is other than wealth." This is shown by the fact that the permission of spoils was not granted to any nation other than this Ummah; rather, it is among its distinguishing features, as he ﷺ said in the hadith agreed upon as authentic: "Spoils have been made lawful for me, and they were not lawful for anyone before me."

Allah, glorified is He, had made lawful the land that was in the hands of the disbelievers for those before us, the followers of the messengers, when they seized it by force, as He made it lawful for the people of Moses. Hence Moses said to his people: ﴿O my people, enter the holy land which Allah has prescribed for you, and do not turn back on your heels, lest you turn about as losers﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 21].

Moses and his people fought the disbelievers, seized their lands and wealth, and gathered the spoils; then fire came down from heaven and consumed them, and they dwelt in the land and the homes, and these were not forbidden to them. It is thus known that land is not among the spoils, and that it belongs to Allah, Who bequeaths it to whom He wills.
